title: How did Rome last until fourteen fifty-three?

post.caption: Ancient Rome, episode 15 (finale): the Roman Empire did not end in Rome. It ended on 29 May 1453 in Constantinople, today's Istanbul, with the last emperor, Constantine XI. Images: public domain (Theophilos, Fossati & Haghe, Gentile Bellini, Jean Le Tavernier, Fausto Zonaro, Library of Congress photochroms, Biblioteca Estense). Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The Roman Empire didn't end in Rome. It ended in Istanbul, in 1453.
beats.say: The Roman Empire didn't end in Rome. It ended in Istanbul, in fourteen fifty-three.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How did Rome last until 1453?
beats.say: How did Rome last until fourteen fifty-three?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In Istanbul today, almost six kilometres of ancient walls still cross the city. In 1453, they protected the last Roman emperor.
beats.say: In Istanbul today, almost six kilometres of ancient walls still cross the city. In fourteen fifty-three, they protected the last Roman emperor.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Wasn't that the Byzantine Empire?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: That's a name historians gave it later. Its people called themselves Romans, and their capital was the city Constantine had founded.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who was the last emperor?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Constantine XI. Like the founder of the city, he was called Constantine, and like him, his mother was called Helena.
beats.say: Constantine the Eleventh. Like the founder of the city, he was called Constantine, and like him, his mother was called Helena.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How much was left of his empire?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Almost nothing: the city and some land in southern Greece. All around it, the Ottoman Empire.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In April 1453, the young sultan Mehmed II arrived with a huge army and giant cannons. Inside, about 7,000 defenders.
beats.say: In April fourteen fifty-three, the young sultan Mehmed the Second arrived with a huge army and giant cannons. Inside, about seven thousand defenders.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How long did they hold out?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: 53 days. Mehmed even had his ships dragged overland, around the chain that closed the harbour.
beats.say: Fifty-three days. Mehmed even had his ships dragged overland, around the chain that closed the harbour.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Before dawn on 29 May, the final attack broke through.
beats.say: Before dawn on the twenty-ninth of May, the final attack broke through.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And the emperor?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: He died fighting at the walls. His body was never identified.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Greek legend says an angel turned him to marble, and he sleeps beneath the Golden Gate, waiting to return.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So that was the end of Rome?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Of the Roman state, yes. But Mehmed took a new title: Caesar of Rome.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: From a wolf's cave on the Tiber to the walls of Istanbul: twenty-two centuries of Rome.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Like the video and follow History Sketches for more history.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments: which Rome story was your favourite?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Most people think the Roman story ends in Rome itself.
